assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological band theory and its realisation in the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects opened a whole field: topological invariants now organise electronic phases, with protected edge transport observed in HgTe and in magnetic topological insulators. The concept is original, clear and has spread into photonics, cold atoms and mechanics, so its lasting impact is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Kane supplied the Z2 theory (with Mele, who is credited in other entries but not here), Molenkamp led the HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment, and Xue's group realised the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Kane, Molenkamp and Xue form a coherent theory-plus-two-experiments trio; it leaves out Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and Hasan, whose roles I cannot adjudicate from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently for more than a decade across several material platforms, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Omission of Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan makes the credit contestable; priority questions in the theory are not resolved by the supplied entry.
The compound entry combines two experimental effects that could be recognised separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity created moiré quantum materials, an entirely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. Originality and growing impact are high, and the platform lets one study interacting many-body physics with a continuous control parameter.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave the magic-angle prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery. A theory-plus-experiment pair is the cleanest configuration; Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands and Bistritzer's share of the model are real credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the phases, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet fully stable. It is timely rather than late, with some risk of being slightly early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and sample-to-sample variability are unresolved.
Allocation among MacDonald, Bistritzer, Andrei and Jarillo-Herrero is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality are exact relations that extend thermodynamics' second law to small systems far from equilibrium and let free-energy differences be extracted from nonequilibrium work. From a statistical-physics perspective this is a conceptually clean and widely used result, tested in single-molecule pulling experiments, and it has shaped stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Evans and collaborators derived the early fluctuation theorem, Jarzynski derived the equality and Crooks the transient relation. Within the supplied names, Jarzynski and Evans seem the most defensible pair; the entry omits Cohen, Morriss and Gallavotti, whose role in the fluctuation theorem is significant, and Crooks has a genuine claim.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA and molecular-motor studies and has extensive follow-up in stochastic thermodynamics. The ideas are well established, although it is not an observed discovery of new phenomena.
uncertainties: The credited trio omits key contributors such as Cohen, Morriss and Gallavotti, so a fair prize may be impossible.
Whether the physics community regards this as a discovery rather than a theoretical framework is subject to judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices have become quantum simulators in which Hubbard-type many-body models can be realised and probed with single-site resolution, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition. Importance is high both for many-body physics and for quantum technology, and the conceptual clarity is good.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger demonstrated the Mott transition and later quantum-gas microscopy. Five names are credited, so choosing three means omitting Cirac, Esslinger or others, a real allocation problem. Zoller, Bloch and Greiner is a reasonable theory-plus-experiment choice.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and widely reproduced across many laboratories over two decades. Timing is mature, but adjacent recognition for ultracold gases and for quantum information in recent years complicates the case.
uncertainties: Allocation among Zoller, Cirac, Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger is contested.
Overlap with other ultracold-atom and quantum-information entries could split the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks combine Katori's magic-wavelength proposal with Ye's work on strontium clocks to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, which supports tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The importance is high and the impact is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: The credited list contains exactly two names; Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove its precision implementation. This is a fair configuration, although Hall, Hänsch and optical-comb contributors (already recognised in 2005) are part of the background.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple national metrology institutes with consistent agreement; stable and mature. Recognition appears timely, with redefinition of the second ahead.
uncertainties: Not clear that the committee treats clocks as a discovery rather than a technology refinement.
Other contributors to ion clocks and lattice-clock spin-squeezing are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnelled energy landscape picture, rooted in spin-glass and random-energy-model ideas, explains how proteins fold quickly by minimal frustration. It is a statistical-physics concept applied to biology, of lasting conceptual value, and I find it compelling from the complex-systems perspective.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson developed the landscape theory; Dill's contributions on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models are distinct. Wolynes and Onuchic is the best fit, though Dill's omission and the chemistry flavour of the field are concerns.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and corroborated through simulations and experiments, yet the work is partly a conceptual framework rather than a single decisive observation. AlphaFold-type successes already received a Chemistry prize in 2024, which affects how a physics prize would be viewed.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics or chemistry for the prize remit is uncertain.
Dill's contribution and Bryngelson's omission raise attribution questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a platform for strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons and underpins superconducting quantum computing. Importance and originality are high, and the field has grown dramatically.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the circuit-QED architecture, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The trio of theory and two experimenters is coherent; Devoret, Martinis and Nakamura are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced widely. The 2025 prize to macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes a quick second recognition in the same area less likely, so timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Closeness to the most recent prize on superconducting circuits may reduce the case.
The prize configuration omits several of the people with earlier decisive contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the later association with a blazar, opened neutrino astronomy, which is a major experimental achievement with broad significance for astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Only Halzen is credited, although IceCube is a collaboration of hundreds and the project depended on the efforts of many scientists. A one-person prize would face a serious fairness question and I cannot confirm from the supplied text who else should share it.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed and the blazar and Galactic-plane evidence is growing, but the identification of the dominant sources is still incomplete. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Narrow credit list for a large collaboration makes attribution weak.
Source identification of the bulk of the neutrino flux remains open.
